persona_label: T4 paraplegic — wheelchair racer and basketball player

conversation_log.content:
To start our conversation, how would you describe your primary approach to movement and training in your daily life?
Options: [High-intensity, structured training aimed at testing my physical limits | Consistent, rhythmic endurance training for sustained performance and mental clarity | Technical, skill-based practice focused on precision and coordination]
High-intensity, structured training aimed at testing my physical limits

When you engage in that level of high-intensity training, what type of environment do you find brings out your best performance?
Options: [Individual pursuit: I prefer to rely solely on my own discipline and mental focus. | Team dynamic: I thrive on collaboration, shared goals, and intense communication. | Tactical competition: I enjoy analyzing opponents and executing complex, high-pressure game plans.]
Tactical competition: I enjoy analyzing opponents and executing complex, high-pressure game plans.

Looking back at your sporting journey so far, where did you first cultivate this ability to deconstruct an opponent's strategy and thrive under pressure?
Options: [Field-based team sports: I learned to read the pitch and coordinate tactical shifts with teammates. | Combat sports or martial arts: I developed the ability to analyze an opponent's physical cues and react instantly. | Racket or court sports: I mastered the art of precision and mental pattern-recognition during high-stakes rallies.]
Field-based team sports: I learned to read the pitch and coordinate tactical shifts with teammates.

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Your background in the high-intensity, structured nature of field-based team sports provides the perfect foundation for the Road Machine archetype. At 163cm and 55kg, you possess a power-to-weight ratio that is inherently efficient for long-distance efforts, allowing you to sustain the high-intensity cadence required to break away from a pack. You have learned to channel the chaotic energy of the pitch into a singular, unwavering focus—the kind of discipline that defines a champion at The Games.

Within the adaptive pathway, the H3 classification specifically serves athletes with an impairment in the lower limbs or trunk who compete using hand-cranked cycles. For a competitor like you, this classification is not merely a technical designation; it is a mechanical extension of your tactical mind. While others might rely solely on raw output, your experience reading the movement of teammates and opponents allows you to navigate the pack with precision, transforming the handcycle into an instrument of pure strategic velocity. You are no longer just running a play; you are dictating the rhythm of the road.

The Mat Technician profile is built for the athlete who views competition as a high-stakes chess match played at full speed. Your history in team sports has equipped you with the ability to deconstruct an opponent's positioning in real-time, an invaluable skill when standing on the mat. You don't just react; you anticipate the opening, closing the distance with the same tactical intensity you once used to control the flow of a game. At The Games, where margins are measured in fractions of a second, your ability to remain analytical under extreme pressure becomes your most lethal weapon.

When we pivot to the adaptive pathway of powerlifting, we strip away the movement of the field and replace it with the intense, localized force of the platform. Here, the challenge is internal and absolute. While your standing pathway in wrestling focuses on reading the opponent, your adaptive pathway demands a mastery of biomechanical precision and explosive force. You will apply the same tactical deconstruction—previously used to out-maneuver a defender—to your own lifting technique, obsessively refining your form to extract every ounce of potential. This transition allows you to express your competitive nature through a different lens: the brutal, honest, and singular pursuit of peak strength.
